msearch-index.name: index
msearch-index.description: Comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and index aliases to search.

msearch-allow_no_indices.name: allow_no_indices
msearch-allow_no_indices.description: If false, the request returns an error if any wildcard expression, index alias, or _all value targets only missing or closed indices. This behavior applies even if the request targets other open indices. For example, a request targeting foo*,bar* returns an error if an index starts with foo but no index starts with bar.

msearch-ccs_minimize_roundtrips.name: ccs_minimize_roundtrips
msearch-ccs_minimize_roundtrips.description: If true, network roundtrips between the coordinating node and remote clusters are minimized for cross-cluster search requests.

msearch-expand_wildcards.name: expand_wildcards
msearch-expand_wildcards.description:
Type of index that wildcard expressions can match. If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.

Supported values include:
  - `all`: Match any data stream or index, including hidden ones.
  - `open`: Match open, non-hidden indices. Also matches any non-hidden data stream.
  - `closed`: Match closed, non-hidden indices. Also matches any non-hidden data stream. Data streams cannot be closed.
  - `hidden`: Match hidden data streams and hidden indices. Must be combined with `open`, `closed`, or `both`.
  - `none`: Wildcard expressions are not accepted.

msearch-ignore_throttled.name: ignore_throttled
msearch-ignore_throttled.description: If true, concrete, expanded or aliased indices are ignored when frozen.

msearch-ignore_unavailable.name: ignore_unavailable
msearch-ignore_unavailable.description: If true, missing or closed indices are not included in the response.

msearch-include_named_queries_score.name: include_named_queries_score
msearch-include_named_queries_score.description:
Indicates whether hit.matched_queries should be rendered as a map that includes
the name of the matched query associated with its score (true)
or as an array containing the name of the matched queries (false)
This functionality reruns each named query on every hit in a search response.
Typically, this adds a small overhead to a request.
However, using computationally expensive named queries on a large number of hits may add significant overhead.

msearch-index_.name: index
msearch-index_.description: Comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and index aliases to use as default

msearch-max_concurrent_searches.name: max_concurrent_searches
msearch-max_concurrent_searches.description:
Maximum number of concurrent searches the multi search API can execute.
Defaults to `max(1, (# of data nodes * min(search thread pool size, 10)))`.

msearch-max_concurrent_shard_requests.name: max_concurrent_shard_requests
msearch-max_concurrent_shard_requests.description: Maximum number of concurrent shard requests that each sub-search request executes per node.

msearch-pre_filter_shard_size.name: pre_filter_shard_size
msearch-pre_filter_shard_size.description: Defines a threshold that enforces a pre-filter roundtrip to prefilter search shards based on query rewriting if the number of shards the search request expands to exceeds the threshold. This filter roundtrip can limit the number of shards significantly if for instance a shard can not match any documents based on its rewrite method i.e., if date filters are mandatory to match but the shard bounds and the query are disjoint.

msearch-rest_total_hits_as_int.name: rest_total_hits_as_int
msearch-rest_total_hits_as_int.description: If true, hits.total are returned as an integer in the response. Defaults to false, which returns an object.

msearch-routing.name: routing
msearch-routing.description: Custom routing value used to route search operations to a specific shard.

msearch-search_type.name: search_type
msearch-search_type.description:
Indicates whether global term and document frequencies should be used when scoring returned documents.

Supported values include:
  - `query_then_fetch`: Documents are scored using local term and document frequencies for the shard. This is usually faster but less accurate.
  - `dfs_query_then_fetch`: Documents are scored using global term and document frequencies across all shards. This is usually slower but more accurate.

msearch-typed_keys.name: typed_keys
msearch-typed_keys.description: Specifies whether aggregation and suggester names should be prefixed by their respective types in the response.

msearch_template-index.name: index
msearch_template-index.description:
A comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and aliases to search.
It supports wildcards (`*`).
To search all data streams and indices, omit this parameter or use `*`.

msearch_template-ccs_minimize_roundtrips.name: ccs_minimize_roundtrips
msearch_template-ccs_minimize_roundtrips.description: If `true`, network round-trips are minimized for cross-cluster search requests.

msearch_template-max_concurrent_searches.name: max_concurrent_searches
msearch_template-max_concurrent_searches.description: The maximum number of concurrent searches the API can run.

msearch_template-search_type.name: search_type
msearch_template-search_type.description:
The type of the search operation.

Supported values include:
  - `query_then_fetch`: Documents are scored using local term and document frequencies for the shard. This is usually faster but less accurate.
  - `dfs_query_then_fetch`: Documents are scored using global term and document frequencies across all shards. This is usually slower but more accurate.

msearch_template-rest_total_hits_as_int.name: rest_total_hits_as_int
msearch_template-rest_total_hits_as_int.description:
If `true`, the response returns `hits.total` as an integer.
If `false`, it returns `hits.total` as an object.

msearch_template-typed_keys.name: typed_keys
msearch_template-typed_keys.description: If `true`, the response prefixes aggregation and suggester names with their respective types.

mtermvectors-index.name: index
mtermvectors-index.description: The name of the index that contains the documents.

mtermvectors-ids.name: ids
mtermvectors-ids.description: A comma-separated list of documents ids. You must define ids as parameter or set "ids" or "docs" in the request body

mtermvectors-fields.name: fields
mtermvectors-fields.description:
A comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in the statistics.
It is used as the default list unless a specific field list is provided in the `completion_fields` or `fielddata_fields` parameters.

mtermvectors-field_statistics.name: field_statistics
mtermvectors-field_statistics.description: If `true`, the response includes the document count, sum of document frequencies, and sum of total term frequencies.

mtermvectors-offsets.name: offsets
mtermvectors-offsets.description: If `true`, the response includes term offsets.

mtermvectors-payloads.name: payloads
mtermvectors-payloads.description: If `true`, the response includes term payloads.

mtermvectors-positions.name: positions
mtermvectors-positions.description: If `true`, the response includes term positions.

mtermvectors-preference.name: preference
mtermvectors-preference.description:
The node or shard the operation should be performed on.
It is random by default.

mtermvectors-realtime.name: realtime
mtermvectors-realtime.description: If true, the request is real-time as opposed to near-real-time.

mtermvectors-routing.name: routing
mtermvectors-routing.description: A custom value used to route operations to a specific shard.

mtermvectors-term_statistics.name: term_statistics
mtermvectors-term_statistics.description: If true, the response includes term frequency and document frequency.

mtermvectors-version.name: version
mtermvectors-version.description: If `true`, returns the document version as part of a hit.

mtermvectors-version_type.name: version_type
mtermvectors-version_type.description:
The version type.

Supported values include:
  - `internal`: Use internal versioning that starts at 1 and increments with each update or delete.
  - `external`: Only index the document if the specified version is strictly higher than the version of the stored document or if there is no existing document.
  - `external_gte`: Only index the document if the specified version is equal or higher than the version of the stored document or if there is no existing document.
NOTE: The `external_gte` version type is meant for special use cases and should be used with care.
If used incorrectly, it can result in loss of data.
  - `force`: This option is deprecated because it can cause primary and replica shards to diverge.

nodes.hot_threads-node_id.name: node_id
nodes.hot_threads-node_id.description: List of node IDs or names used to limit returned information.

nodes.hot_threads-ignore_idle_threads.name: ignore_idle_threads
nodes.hot_threads-ignore_idle_threads.description:
If true, known idle threads (e.g. waiting in a socket select, or to get
a task from an empty queue) are filtered out.

nodes.hot_threads-interval.name: interval
nodes.hot_threads-interval.description: The interval to do the second sampling of threads.

nodes.hot_threads-snapshots.name: snapshots
nodes.hot_threads-snapshots.description: Number of samples of thread stacktrace.

nodes.hot_threads-threads.name: threads
nodes.hot_threads-threads.description: Specifies the number of hot threads to provide information for.

nodes.hot_threads-timeout.name: timeout
nodes.hot_threads-timeout.description:
Period to wait for a response. If no response is received
before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.

nodes.hot_threads-sort.name: sort
nodes.hot_threads-sort.description: The sort order for 'cpu' type (default: total)

nodes.info-node_id.name: node_id
nodes.info-node_id.description: Comma-separated list of node IDs or names used to limit returned information.

nodes.info-metric.name: metric
nodes.info-metric.description: Limits the information returned to the specific metrics. Supports a comma-separated list, such as http,ingest.

nodes.info-flat_settings.name: flat_settings
nodes.info-flat_settings.description: If true, returns settings in flat format.

nodes.info-timeout.name: timeout
nodes.info-timeout.description: Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.

nodes.reload_secure_settings-node_id.name: node_id
nodes.reload_secure_settings-node_id.description: The names of particular nodes in the cluster to target.

nodes.reload_secure_settings-timeout.name: timeout
nodes.reload_secure_settings-timeout.description:
Period to wait for a response.
If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.

nodes.stats-node_id.name: node_id
nodes.stats-node_id.description: Comma-separated list of node IDs or names used to limit returned information.

nodes.stats-metric.name: metric
nodes.stats-metric.description: Limit the information returned to the specified metrics

nodes.stats-index_metric.name: index_metric
nodes.stats-index_metric.description: Limit the information returned for indices metric to the specific index metrics. It can be used only if indices (or all) metric is specified.

nodes.stats-completion_fields.name: completion_fields
nodes.stats-completion_fields.description: Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in fielddata and suggest statistics.

nodes.stats-fielddata_fields.name: fielddata_fields
nodes.stats-fielddata_fields.description: Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in fielddata statistics.

nodes.stats-fields.name: fields
nodes.stats-fields.description: Comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in the statistics.

nodes.stats-groups.name: groups
nodes.stats-groups.description: Comma-separated list of search groups to include in the search statistics.

nodes.stats-include_segment_file_sizes.name: include_segment_file_sizes
nodes.stats-include_segment_file_sizes.description: If true, the call reports the aggregated disk usage of each one of the Lucene index files (only applies if segment stats are requested).

nodes.stats-level.name: level
nodes.stats-level.description: Indicates whether statistics are aggregated at the cluster, index, or shard level.

nodes.stats-timeout.name: timeout
nodes.stats-timeout.description: Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.

nodes.stats-types.name: types
nodes.stats-types.description: A comma-separated list of document types for the indexing index metric.

nodes.stats-include_unloaded_segments.name: include_unloaded_segments
nodes.stats-include_unloaded_segments.description: If `true`, the response includes information from segments that are not loaded into memory.

nodes.usage-node_id.name: node_id
nodes.usage-node_id.description: A comma-separated list of node IDs or names to limit the returned information; use `_local` to return information from the node you're connecting to, leave empty to get information from all nodes

nodes.usage-metric.name: metric
nodes.usage-metric.description:
Limits the information returned to the specific metrics.
A comma-separated list of the following options: `_all`, `rest_actions`.

nodes.usage-timeout.name: timeout
nodes.usage-timeout.description:
Period to wait for a response.
If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.

put_script-id.name: id
put_script-id.description:
The identifier for the stored script or search template.
It must be unique within the cluster.

put_script-context.name: context
put_script-context.description:
The context in which the script or search template should run.
To prevent errors, the API immediately compiles the script or template in this context.

put_script-context_.name: context
put_script-context_.description:
The context in which the script or search template should run.
To prevent errors, the API immediately compiles the script or template in this context.
If you specify both this and the `<context>` path parameter, the API uses the request path parameter.

put_script-master_timeout.name: master_timeout
put_script-master_timeout.description:
The period to wait for a connection to the master node.
If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.
It can also be set to `-1` to indicate that the request should never timeout.

put_script-timeout.name: timeout
put_script-timeout.description:
The period to wait for a response.
If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.
It can also be set to `-1` to indicate that the request should never timeout.

rank_eval-index.name: index
rank_eval-index.description:
A  comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and index aliases used to limit the request.
Wildcard (`*`) expressions are supported.
To target all data streams and indices in a cluster, omit this parameter or use `_all` or `*`.

rank_eval-allow_no_indices.name: allow_no_indices
rank_eval-allow_no_indices.description: If `false`, the request returns an error if any wildcard expression, index alias, or `_all` value targets only missing or closed indices. This behavior applies even if the request targets other open indices. For example, a request targeting `foo*,bar*` returns an error if an index starts with `foo` but no index starts with `bar`.

rank_eval-expand_wildcards.name: expand_wildcards
rank_eval-expand_wildcards.description:
Whether to expand wildcard expression to concrete indices that are open, closed or both.

Supported values include:
  - `all`: Match any data stream or index, including hidden ones.
  - `open`: Match open, non-hidden indices. Also matches any non-hidden data stream.
  - `closed`: Match closed, non-hidden indices. Also matches any non-hidden data stream. Data streams cannot be closed.
  - `hidden`: Match hidden data streams and hidden indices. Must be combined with `open`, `closed`, or `both`.
  - `none`: Wildcard expressions are not accepted.

rank_eval-ignore_unavailable.name: ignore_unavailable
rank_eval-ignore_unavailable.description: If `true`, missing or closed indices are not included in the response.

render_search_template-id.name: id
render_search_template-id.description:
The ID of the search template to render.
If no `source` is specified, this or the `id` request body parameter is required.

rollup.get_jobs-id.name: id
rollup.get_jobs-id.description:
Identifier for the rollup job.
If it is `_all` or omitted, the API returns all rollup jobs.

rollup.get_rollup_caps-id.name: id
rollup.get_rollup_caps-id.description:
Index, indices or index-pattern to return rollup capabilities for.
`_all` may be used to fetch rollup capabilities from all jobs.

rollup.rollup_search-index.name: index
rollup.rollup_search-index.description:
A comma-separated list of data streams and indices used to limit the request.
This parameter has the following rules:

* At least one data stream, index, or wildcard expression must be specified. This target can include a rollup or non-rollup index. For data streams, the stream's backing indices can only serve as non-rollup indices. Omitting the parameter or using `_all` are not permitted.
* Multiple non-rollup indices may be specified.
* Only one rollup index may be specified. If more than one are supplied, an exception occurs.
* Wildcard expressions (`*`) may be used. If they match more than one rollup index, an exception occurs. However, you can use an expression to match multiple non-rollup indices or data streams.

rollup.rollup_search-rest_total_hits_as_.name: rest_total_hits_as_int
rollup.rollup_search-rest_total_hits_as_.description: Indicates whether hits.total should be rendered as an integer or an object in the rest search response

rollup.rollup_search-typed_keys.name: typed_keys
rollup.rollup_search-typed_keys.description: Specify whether aggregation and suggester names should be prefixed by their respective types in the response

scroll-scroll.name: scroll
scroll-scroll.description: The period to retain the search context for scrolling.

scroll-scroll_id_.name: scroll_id
scroll-scroll_id_.description: The scroll ID for scrolled search

scroll-rest_total_hits_as_int.name: rest_total_hits_as_int
scroll-rest_total_hits_as_int.description: If true, the API response’s hit.total property is returned as an integer. If false, the API response’s hit.total property is returned as an object.

search-index.name: index
search-index.description:
A comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and aliases to search.
It supports wildcards (`*`).
To search all data streams and indices, omit this parameter or use `*` or `_all`.

search-allow_no_indices.name: allow_no_indices
search-allow_no_indices.description:
If `false`, the request returns an error if any wildcard expression, index alias, or `_all` value targets only missing or closed indices.
This behavior applies even if the request targets other open indices.
For example, a request targeting `foo*,bar*` returns an error if an index starts with `foo` but no index starts with `bar`.

search-allow_partial_search_results.name: allow_partial_search_results
search-allow_partial_search_results.description:
If `true` and there are shard request timeouts or shard failures, the request returns partial results.
If `false`, it returns an error with no partial results.

To override the default behavior, you can set the `search.default_allow_partial_results` cluster setting to `false`.

search-analyzer.name: analyzer
search-analyzer.description:
The analyzer to use for the query string.
This parameter can be used only when the `q` query string parameter is specified.

search-analyze_wildcard.name: analyze_wildcard
search-analyze_wildcard.description:
If `true`, wildcard and prefix queries are analyzed.
This parameter can be used only when the `q` query string parameter is specified.

search-batched_reduce_size.name: batched_reduce_size
search-batched_reduce_size.description:
The number of shard results that should be reduced at once on the coordinating node.
If the potential number of shards in the request can be large, this value should be used as a protection mechanism to reduce the memory overhead per search request.

search-ccs_minimize_roundtrips.name: ccs_minimize_roundtrips
search-ccs_minimize_roundtrips.description: If `true`, network round-trips between the coordinating node and the remote clusters are minimized when running cross-cluster search (CCS) requests.

search-default_operator.name: default_operator
search-default_operator.description:
The default operator for the query string query: `AND` or `OR`.
This parameter can be used only when the `q` query string parameter is specified.

search-df.name: df
search-df.description:
The field to use as a default when no field prefix is given in the query string.
This parameter can be used only when the `q` query string parameter is specified.

search-docvalue_fields.name: docvalue_fields
search-docvalue_fields.description: A comma-separated list of fields to return as the docvalue representation of a field for each hit.

search-expand_wildcards.name: expand_wildcards
search-expand_wildcards.description:
The type of index that wildcard patterns can match.
If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.
It supports comma-separated values such as `open,hidden`.

Supported values include:
  - `all`: Match any data stream or index, including hidden ones.
  - `open`: Match open, non-hidden indices. Also matches any non-hidden data stream.
  - `closed`: Match closed, non-hidden indices. Also matches any non-hidden data stream. Data streams cannot be closed.
  - `hidden`: Match hidden data streams and hidden indices. Must be combined with `open`, `closed`, or `both`.
  - `none`: Wildcard expressions are not accepted.

search-explain.name: explain
search-explain.description: If `true`, the request returns detailed information about score computation as part of a hit.

search-ignore_throttled.name: ignore_throttled
search-ignore_throttled.description: If `true`, concrete, expanded or aliased indices will be ignored when frozen.

search-ignore_unavailable.name: ignore_unavailable
search-ignore_unavailable.description: If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a missing or closed index.

search-include_named_queries_score.name: include_named_queries_score
search-include_named_queries_score.description:
If `true`, the response includes the score contribution from any named queries.

This functionality reruns each named query on every hit in a search response.
Typically, this adds a small overhead to a request.
However, using computationally expensive named queries on a large number of hits may add significant overhead.

search-lenient.name: lenient
search-lenient.description:
If `true`, format-based query failures (such as providing text to a numeric field) in the query string will be ignored.
This parameter can be used only when the `q` query string parameter is specified.

search-max_concurrent_shard_requests.name: max_concurrent_shard_requests
search-max_concurrent_shard_requests.description:
The number of concurrent shard requests per node that the search runs concurrently.
This value should be used to limit the impact of the search on the cluster in order to limit the number of concurrent shard requests.

search-preference.name: preference
search-preference.description:
The nodes and shards used for the search.
By default, Elasticsearch selects from eligible nodes and shards using adaptive replica selection, accounting for allocation awareness.
Valid values are:

* `_only_local` to run the search only on shards on the local node.
* `_local` to, if possible, run the search on shards on the local node, or if not, select shards using the default method.
* `_only_nodes:<node-id>,<node-id>` to run the search on only the specified nodes IDs. If suitable shards exist on more than one selected node, use shards on those nodes using the default method. If none of the specified nodes are available, select shards from any available node using the default method.
* `_prefer_nodes:<node-id>,<node-id>` to if possible, run the search on the specified nodes IDs. If not, select shards using the default method.
* `_shards:<shard>,<shard>` to run the search only on the specified shards. You can combine this value with other `preference` values. However, the `_shards` value must come first. For example: `_shards:2,3|_local`.
* `<custom-string>` (any string that does not start with `_`) to route searches with the same `<custom-string>` to the same shards in the same order.

search-pre_filter_shard_size.name: pre_filter_shard_size
search-pre_filter_shard_size.description:
A threshold that enforces a pre-filter roundtrip to prefilter search shards based on query rewriting if the number of shards the search request expands to exceeds the threshold.
This filter roundtrip can limit the number of shards significantly if for instance a shard can not match any documents based on its rewrite method (if date filters are mandatory to match but the shard bounds and the query are disjoint).
When unspecified, the pre-filter phase is executed if any of these conditions is met:

* The request targets more than 128 shards.
* The request targets one or more read-only index.
* The primary sort of the query targets an indexed field.

search-request_cache.name: request_cache
search-request_cache.description:
If `true`, the caching of search results is enabled for requests where `size` is `0`.
It defaults to index level settings.

search-routing.name: routing
search-routing.description: A custom value that is used to route operations to a specific shard.

search-scroll.name: scroll
search-scroll.description:
The period to retain the search context for scrolling.
By default, this value cannot exceed `1d` (24 hours).
You can change this limit by using the `search.max_keep_alive` cluster-level setting.

search-search_type.name: search_type
search-search_type.description:
Indicates how distributed term frequencies are calculated for relevance scoring.

Supported values include:
  - `query_then_fetch`: Documents are scored using local term and document frequencies for the shard. This is usually faster but less accurate.
  - `dfs_query_then_fetch`: Documents are scored using global term and document frequencies across all shards. This is usually slower but more accurate.

search-stats.name: stats
search-stats.description: Specific `tag` of the request for logging and statistical purposes.

search-stored_fields.name: stored_fields
search-stored_fields.description:
A comma-separated list of stored fields to return as part of a hit.
If no fields are specified, no stored fields are included in the response.
If this field is specified, the `_source` parameter defaults to `false`.
You can pass `_source: true` to return both source fields and stored fields in the search response.

search-suggest_field.name: suggest_field
search-suggest_field.description: The field to use for suggestions.

search-suggest_mode.name: suggest_mode
search-suggest_mode.description:
The suggest mode.
This parameter can be used only when the `suggest_field` and `suggest_text` query string parameters are specified.

Supported values include:
  - `missing`: Only generate suggestions for terms that are not in the shard.
  - `popular`: Only suggest terms that occur in more docs on the shard than the original term.
  - `always`: Suggest any matching suggestions based on terms in the suggest text.

search-suggest_size.name: suggest_size
search-suggest_size.description:
The number of suggestions to return.
This parameter can be used only when the `suggest_field` and `suggest_text` query string parameters are specified.

search-suggest_text.name: suggest_text
search-suggest_text.description:
The source text for which the suggestions should be returned.
This parameter can be used only when the `suggest_field` and `suggest_text` query string parameters are specified.

search-terminate_after.name: terminate_after
search-terminate_after.description:
The maximum number of documents to collect for each shard.
If a query reaches this limit, Elasticsearch terminates the query early.
Elasticsearch collects documents before sorting.

IMPORTANT: Use with caution.
Elasticsearch applies this parameter to each shard handling the request.
When possible, let Elasticsearch perform early termination automatically.
Avoid specifying this parameter for requests that target data streams with backing indices across multiple data tiers.
If set to `0` (default), the query does not terminate early.

search-timeout.name: timeout
search-timeout.description:
The period of time to wait for a response from each shard.
If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.
It defaults to no timeout.

search-track_total_hits.name: track_total_hits
search-track_total_hits.description:
The number of hits matching the query to count accurately.
If `true`, the exact number of hits is returned at the cost of some performance.
If `false`, the response does not include the total number of hits matching the query.

search-track_scores.name: track_scores
search-track_scores.description: If `true`, the request calculates and returns document scores, even if the scores are not used for sorting.

search-typed_keys.name: typed_keys
search-typed_keys.description: If `true`, aggregation and suggester names are be prefixed by their respective types in the response.

search-rest_total_hits_as_int.name: rest_total_hits_as_int
search-rest_total_hits_as_int.description: Indicates whether `hits.total` should be rendered as an integer or an object in the rest search response.

search-version.name: version
search-version.description: If `true`, the request returns the document version as part of a hit.

search-_source.name: _source
search-_source.description:
The source fields that are returned for matching documents.
These fields are returned in the `hits._source` property of the search response.
Valid values are:

* `true` to return the entire document source.
* `false` to not return the document source.
* `<string>` to return the source fields that are specified as a comma-separated list that supports wildcard (`*`) patterns.

search-_source_excludes.name: _source_excludes
search-_source_excludes.description:
A comma-separated list of source fields to exclude from the response.
You can also use this parameter to exclude fields from the subset specified in `_source_includes` query parameter.
If the `_source` parameter is `false`, this parameter is ignored.

search-_source_exclude_vectors.name: _source_exclude_vectors
search-_source_exclude_vectors.description: Whether vectors should be excluded from _source

search-_source_includes.name: _source_includes
search-_source_includes.description:
A comma-separated list of source fields to include in the response.
If this parameter is specified, only these source fields are returned.
You can exclude fields from this subset using the `_source_excludes` query parameter.
If the `_source` parameter is `false`, this parameter is ignored.

search-seq_no_primary_term.name: seq_no_primary_term
search-seq_no_primary_term.description: If `true`, the request returns the sequence number and primary term of the last modification of each hit.

search-q.name: q
search-q.description:
A query in the Lucene query string syntax.
Query parameter searches do not support the full Elasticsearch Query DSL but are handy for testing.

IMPORTANT: This parameter overrides the query parameter in the request body.
If both parameters are specified, documents matching the query request body parameter are not returned.

search-size.name: size
search-size.description:
The number of hits to return.
By default, you cannot page through more than 10,000 hits using the `from` and `size` parameters.
To page through more hits, use the `search_after` parameter.

search-from.name: from
search-from.description:
The starting document offset, which must be non-negative.
By default, you cannot page through more than 10,000 hits using the `from` and `size` parameters.
To page through more hits, use the `search_after` parameter.

search_application.get_behavioral_analyt.name: name
search_application.get_behavioral_analyt.description: A list of analytics collections to limit the returned information

search_application.search-name.name: name
search_application.search-name.description: The name of the search application to be searched.

search_application.search-typed_keys.name: typed_keys
search_application.search-typed_keys.description: Determines whether aggregation names are prefixed by their respective types in the response.

search_mvt-index.name: index
search_mvt-index.description: Comma-separated list of data streams, indices, or aliases to search

search_mvt-field.name: field
search_mvt-field.description: Field containing geospatial data to return

search_mvt-zoom.name: zoom
search_mvt-zoom.description: Zoom level for the vector tile to search

search_mvt-x.name: x
search_mvt-x.description: X coordinate for the vector tile to search

search_mvt-y.name: y
search_mvt-y.description: Y coordinate for the vector tile to search

search_mvt-exact_bounds.name: exact_bounds
search_mvt-exact_bounds.description:
If `false`, the meta layer's feature is the bounding box of the tile.
If true, the meta layer's feature is a bounding box resulting from a
geo_bounds aggregation. The aggregation runs on <field> values that intersect
the <zoom>/<x>/<y> tile with wrap_longitude set to false. The resulting
bounding box may be larger than the vector tile.

search_mvt-extent.name: extent
search_mvt-extent.description: The size, in pixels, of a side of the tile. Vector tiles are square with equal sides.

search_mvt-grid_agg.name: grid_agg
search_mvt-grid_agg.description: Aggregation used to create a grid for `field`.

search_mvt-grid_precision.name: grid_precision
search_mvt-grid_precision.description:
Additional zoom levels available through the aggs layer. For example, if <zoom> is 7
and grid_precision is 8, you can zoom in up to level 15. Accepts 0-8. If 0, results
don't include the aggs layer.

search_mvt-grid_type.name: grid_type
search_mvt-grid_type.description:
Determines the geometry type for features in the aggs layer. In the aggs layer,
each feature represents a geotile_grid cell. If 'grid' each feature is a Polygon
of the cells bounding box. If 'point' each feature is a Point that is the centroid
of the cell.

search_mvt-size.name: size
search_mvt-size.description:
Maximum number of features to return in the hits layer. Accepts 0-10000.
If 0, results don't include the hits layer.

search_mvt-track_total_hits.name: track_total_hits
search_mvt-track_total_hits.description:
The number of hits matching the query to count accurately.
If `true`, the exact number of hits is returned at the cost of some performance.
If `false`, the response does not include the total number of hits matching the query.

search_mvt-with_labels.name: with_labels
search_mvt-with_labels.description:
If `true`, the hits and aggs layers will contain additional point features representing
suggested label positions for the original features.

* `Point` and `MultiPoint` features will have one of the points selected.
* `Polygon` and `MultiPolygon` features will have a single point generated, either the centroid, if it is within the polygon, or another point within the polygon selected from the sorted triangle-tree.
* `LineString` features will likewise provide a roughly central point selected from the triangle-tree.
* The aggregation results will provide one central point for each aggregation bucket.

All attributes from the original features will also be copied to the new label features.
In addition, the new features will be distinguishable using the tag `_mvt_label_position`.

search_shards-index.name: index
search_shards-index.description:
A comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and aliases to search.
It supports wildcards (`*`).
To search all data streams and indices, omit this parameter or use `*` or `_all`.

search_shards-allow_no_indices.name: allow_no_indices
search_shards-allow_no_indices.description:
If `false`, the request returns an error if any wildcard expression, index alias, or `_all` value targets only missing or closed indices.
This behavior applies even if the request targets other open indices.
For example, a request targeting `foo*,bar*` returns an error if an index starts with `foo` but no index starts with `bar`.

search_shards-expand_wildcards.name: expand_wildcards
search_shards-expand_wildcards.description:
Type of index that wildcard patterns can match.
If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.
Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.

Supported values include:
  - `all`: Match any data stream or index, including hidden ones.
  - `open`: Match open, non-hidden indices. Also matches any non-hidden data stream.
  - `closed`: Match closed, non-hidden indices. Also matches any non-hidden data stream. Data streams cannot be closed.
  - `hidden`: Match hidden data streams and hidden indices. Must be combined with `open`, `closed`, or `both`.
  - `none`: Wildcard expressions are not accepted.

search_shards-ignore_unavailable.name: ignore_unavailable
search_shards-ignore_unavailable.description: If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a missing or closed index.

search_shards-local.name: local
search_shards-local.description: If `true`, the request retrieves information from the local node only.

search_shards-master_timeout.name: master_timeout
search_shards-master_timeout.description:
The period to wait for a connection to the master node.
If the master node is not available before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.
IT can also be set to `-1` to indicate that the request should never timeout.

search_shards-preference.name: preference
search_shards-preference.description:
The node or shard the operation should be performed on.
It is random by default.

search_shards-routing.name: routing
search_shards-routing.description: A custom value used to route operations to a specific shard.

search_template-index.name: index
search_template-index.description:
A comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and aliases to search.
It supports wildcards (`*`).

search_template-allow_no_indices.name: allow_no_indices
search_template-allow_no_indices.description:
If `false`, the request returns an error if any wildcard expression, index alias, or `_all` value targets only missing or closed indices.
This behavior applies even if the request targets other open indices.
For example, a request targeting `foo*,bar*` returns an error if an index starts with `foo` but no index starts with `bar`.

search_template-ccs_minimize_roundtrips.name: ccs_minimize_roundtrips
search_template-ccs_minimize_roundtrips.description: If `true`, network round-trips are minimized for cross-cluster search requests.

search_template-expand_wildcards.name: expand_wildcards
search_template-expand_wildcards.description:
The type of index that wildcard patterns can match.
If the request can target data streams, this argument determines whether wildcard expressions match hidden data streams.
Supports comma-separated values, such as `open,hidden`.

Supported values include:
  - `all`: Match any data stream or index, including hidden ones.
  - `open`: Match open, non-hidden indices. Also matches any non-hidden data stream.
  - `closed`: Match closed, non-hidden indices. Also matches any non-hidden data stream. Data streams cannot be closed.
  - `hidden`: Match hidden data streams and hidden indices. Must be combined with `open`, `closed`, or `both`.
  - `none`: Wildcard expressions are not accepted.

search_template-explain.name: explain
search_template-explain.description: If `true`, the response includes additional details about score computation as part of a hit.

search_template-ignore_throttled.name: ignore_throttled
search_template-ignore_throttled.description: If `true`, specified concrete, expanded, or aliased indices are not included in the response when throttled.

search_template-ignore_unavailable.name: ignore_unavailable
search_template-ignore_unavailable.description: If `false`, the request returns an error if it targets a missing or closed index.

search_template-preference.name: preference
search_template-preference.description:
The node or shard the operation should be performed on.
It is random by default.

search_template-profile.name: profile
search_template-profile.description: If `true`, the query execution is profiled.

search_template-routing.name: routing
search_template-routing.description: A custom value used to route operations to a specific shard.

search_template-scroll.name: scroll
search_template-scroll.description:
Specifies how long a consistent view of the index
should be maintained for scrolled search.

search_template-search_type.name: search_type
search_template-search_type.description:
The type of the search operation.

Supported values include:
  - `query_then_fetch`: Documents are scored using local term and document frequencies for the shard. This is usually faster but less accurate.
  - `dfs_query_then_fetch`: Documents are scored using global term and document frequencies across all shards. This is usually slower but more accurate.

search_template-rest_total_hits_as_int.name: rest_total_hits_as_int
search_template-rest_total_hits_as_int.description:
If `true`, `hits.total` is rendered as an integer in the response.
If `false`, it is rendered as an object.

search_template-typed_keys.name: typed_keys
search_template-typed_keys.description: If `true`, the response prefixes aggregation and suggester names with their respective types.

searchable_snapshots.cache_stats-node_id.name: node_id
searchable_snapshots.cache_stats-node_id.description: The names of the nodes in the cluster to target.

searchable_snapshots.clear_cache-index.name: index
searchable_snapshots.clear_cache-index.description:
A comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and aliases to clear from the cache.
It supports wildcards (`*`).

searchable_snapshots.clear_cache-expand_.name: expand_wildcards
searchable_snapshots.clear_cache-expand_.description:
Whether to expand wildcard expression to concrete indices that are open, closed or both.

Supported values include:
  - `all`: Match any data stream or index, including hidden ones.
  - `open`: Match open, non-hidden indices. Also matches any non-hidden data stream.
  - `closed`: Match closed, non-hidden indices. Also matches any non-hidden data stream. Data streams cannot be closed.
  - `hidden`: Match hidden data streams and hidden indices. Must be combined with `open`, `closed`, or `both`.
  - `none`: Wildcard expressions are not accepted.

searchable_snapshots.clear_cache-allow_n.name: allow_no_indices
searchable_snapshots.clear_cache-allow_n.description: Whether to ignore if a wildcard indices expression resolves into no concrete indices. (This includes `_all` string or when no indices have been specified)

searchable_snapshots.clear_cache-ignore_.name: ignore_unavailable
searchable_snapshots.clear_cache-ignore_.description: Whether specified concrete indices should be ignored when unavailable (missing or closed)

searchable_snapshots.stats-index.name: index
searchable_snapshots.stats-index.description: A comma-separated list of data streams and indices to retrieve statistics for.

searchable_snapshots.stats-level.name: level
searchable_snapshots.stats-level.description: Return stats aggregated at cluster, index or shard level

security.change_password-username.name: username
security.change_password-username.description:
The user whose password you want to change. If you do not specify this
parameter, the password is changed for the current user.

security.change_password-refresh.name: refresh
security.change_password-refresh.description: If `true` (the default) then refresh the affected shards to make this operation visible to search, if `wait_for` then wait for a refresh to make this operation visible to search, if `false` then do nothing with refreshes.

security.create_api_key-refresh.name: refresh
security.create_api_key-refresh.description: If `true` (the default) then refresh the affected shards to make this operation visible to search, if `wait_for` then wait for a refresh to make this operation visible to search, if `false` then do nothing with refreshes.

security.create_service_token-namespace.name: namespace
security.create_service_token-namespace.description: The name of the namespace, which is a top-level grouping of service accounts.

security.create_service_token-name.name: name
security.create_service_token-name.description:
The name for the service account token.
If omitted, a random name will be generated.

Token names must be at least one and no more than 256 characters.
They can contain alphanumeric characters (a-z, A-Z, 0-9), dashes (`-`), and underscores (`_`), but cannot begin with an underscore.

NOTE: Token names must be unique in the context of the associated service account.
They must also be globally unique with their fully qualified names, which are comprised of the service account principal and token name, such as `<namespace>/<service>/<token-name>`.

security.create_service_token-refresh.name: refresh
security.create_service_token-refresh.description: If `true` then refresh the affected shards to make this operation visible to search, if `wait_for` (the default) then wait for a refresh to make this operation visible to search, if `false` then do nothing with refreshes.

security.disable_user-refresh.name: refresh
security.disable_user-refresh.description: If `true` (the default) then refresh the affected shards to make this operation visible to search, if `wait_for` then wait for a refresh to make this operation visible to search, if `false` then do nothing with refreshes.

security.disable_user_profile-uid.name: uid
security.disable_user_profile-uid.description: Unique identifier for the user profile.

security.disable_user_profile-refresh.name: refresh
security.disable_user_profile-refresh.description:
If 'true', Elasticsearch refreshes the affected shards to make this operation visible to search.
If 'wait_for', it waits for a refresh to make this operation visible to search.
If 'false', it does nothing with refreshes.

security.enable_user-refresh.name: refresh
security.enable_user-refresh.description: If `true` (the default) then refresh the affected shards to make this operation visible to search, if `wait_for` then wait for a refresh to make this operation visible to search, if `false` then do nothing with refreshes.

security.enable_user_profile-uid.name: uid
security.enable_user_profile-uid.description: A unique identifier for the user profile.

security.enable_user_profile-refresh.name: refresh
security.enable_user_profile-refresh.description:
If 'true', Elasticsearch refreshes the affected shards to make this operation
visible to search.
If 'wait_for', it waits for a refresh to make this operation visible to search.
If 'false', nothing is done with refreshes.

security.get_privileges-application.name: application
security.get_privileges-application.description:
The name of the application.
Application privileges are always associated with exactly one application.
If you do not specify this parameter, the API returns information about all privileges for all applications.

security.get_privileges-name.name: name
security.get_privileges-name.description:
The name of the privilege.
If you do not specify this parameter, the API returns information about all privileges for the requested application.

security.get_role-name.name: name
security.get_role-name.description:
The name of the role.
You can specify multiple roles as a comma-separated list.
If you do not specify this parameter, the API returns information about all roles.

security.get_role_mapping-name.name: name
security.get_role_mapping-name.description: The distinct name that identifies the role mapping. The name is used solely as an identifier to facilitate interaction via the API; it does not affect the behavior of the mapping in any way. You can specify multiple mapping names as a comma-separated list. If you do not specify this parameter, the API returns information about all role mappings.

security.get_service_accounts-namespace.name: namespace
security.get_service_accounts-namespace.description:
The name of the namespace.
Omit this parameter to retrieve information about all service accounts.
If you omit this parameter, you must also omit the `service` parameter.

security.get_service_accounts-service.name: service
security.get_service_accounts-service.description:
The service name.
Omit this parameter to retrieve information about all service accounts that belong to the specified `namespace`.

security.get_user-username.name: username
security.get_user-username.description: An identifier for the user. You can specify multiple usernames as a comma-separated list. If you omit this parameter, the API retrieves information about all users.

security.get_user-with_profile_uid.name: with_profile_uid
security.get_user-with_profile_uid.description: Determines whether to retrieve the user profile UID, if it exists, for the users.

security.put_privileges-refresh.name: refresh
security.put_privileges-refresh.description: If `true` (the default) then refresh the affected shards to make this operation visible to search, if `wait_for` then wait for a refresh to make this operation visible to search, if `false` then do nothing with refreshes.

security.put_role-name.name: name
security.put_role-name.description: The name of the role that is being created or updated. On Elasticsearch Serverless, the role name must begin with a letter or digit and can only contain letters, digits and the characters '_', '-', and '.'. Each role must have a unique name, as this will serve as the identifier for that role.

security.put_role-refresh.name: refresh
security.put_role-refresh.description: If `true` (the default) then refresh the affected shards to make this operation visible to search, if `wait_for` then wait for a refresh to make this operation visible to search, if `false` then do nothing with refreshes.

security.put_role_mapping-name.name: name
security.put_role_mapping-name.description:
The distinct name that identifies the role mapping.
The name is used solely as an identifier to facilitate interaction via the API; it does not affect the behavior of the mapping in any way.

security.put_role_mapping-refresh.name: refresh
security.put_role_mapping-refresh.description: If `true` (the default) then refresh the affected shards to make this operation visible to search, if `wait_for` then wait for a refresh to make this operation visible to search, if `false` then do nothing with refreshes.

security.put_user-username.name: username
security.put_user-username.description:
An identifier for the user.

NOTE: Usernames must be at least 1 and no more than 507 characters.
They can contain alphanumeric characters (a-z, A-Z, 0-9), spaces, punctuation, and printable symbols in the Basic Latin (ASCII) block.
Leading or trailing whitespace is not allowed.

security.put_user-refresh.name: refresh
security.put_user-refresh.description:
Valid values are `true`, `false`, and `wait_for`.
These values have the same meaning as in the index API, but the default value for this API is true.

security.query_api_keys-with_limited_by.name: with_limited_by
security.query_api_keys-with_limited_by.description:
Return the snapshot of the owner user's role descriptors associated with the API key.
An API key's actual permission is the intersection of its assigned role descriptors and the owner user's role descriptors (effectively limited by it).
An API key cannot retrieve any API key’s limited-by role descriptors (including itself) unless it has `manage_api_key` or higher privileges.

security.query_api_keys-with_profile_uid.name: with_profile_uid
security.query_api_keys-with_profile_uid.description:
Determines whether to also retrieve the profile UID for the API key owner principal.
If it exists, the profile UID is returned under the `profile_uid` response field for each API key.

security.query_api_keys-typed_keys.name: typed_keys
security.query_api_keys-typed_keys.description: Determines whether aggregation names are prefixed by their respective types in the response.

security.query_user-with_profile_uid.name: with_profile_uid
security.query_user-with_profile_uid.description: Determines whether to retrieve the user profile UID, if it exists, for the users.

security.suggest_user_profiles-data.name: data
security.suggest_user_profiles-data.description:
A comma-separated list of filters for the `data` field of the profile document.
To return all content use `data=*`.
To return a subset of content, use `data=<key>` to retrieve content nested under the specified `<key>`.
By default, the API returns no `data` content.
It is an error to specify `data` as both the query parameter and the request body field.

security.update_user_profile_data-uid.name: uid
security.update_user_profile_data-uid.description: A unique identifier for the user profile.

security.update_user_profile_data-if_seq.name: if_seq_no
security.update_user_profile_data-if_seq.description: Only perform the operation if the document has this sequence number.

security.update_user_profile_data-if_pri.name: if_primary_term
security.update_user_profile_data-if_pri.description: Only perform the operation if the document has this primary term.

security.update_user_profile_data-refres.name: refresh
security.update_user_profile_data-refres.description:
If 'true', Elasticsearch refreshes the affected shards to make this operation
visible to search.
If 'wait_for', it waits for a refresh to make this operation visible to search.
If 'false', nothing is done with refreshes.

simulate.ingest-index.name: index
simulate.ingest-index.description:
The index to simulate ingesting into.
This value can be overridden by specifying an index on each document.
If you specify this parameter in the request path, it is used for any documents that do not explicitly specify an index argument.

simulate.ingest-pipeline.name: pipeline
simulate.ingest-pipeline.description:
The pipeline to use as the default pipeline.
This value can be used to override the default pipeline of the index.

simulate.ingest-merge_type.name: merge_type
simulate.ingest-merge_type.description:
The mapping merge type if mapping overrides are being provided in mapping_addition.
The allowed values are one of index or template.
The index option merges mappings the way they would be merged into an existing index.
The template option merges mappings the way they would be merged into a template.

slm.get_lifecycle-policy_id.name: policy_id
slm.get_lifecycle-policy_id.description: Comma-separated list of snapshot lifecycle policies to retrieve

slm.get_lifecycle-master_timeout.name: master_timeout
slm.get_lifecycle-master_timeout.description:
The period to wait for a connection to the master node.
If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.

slm.get_lifecycle-timeout.name: timeout
slm.get_lifecycle-timeout.description:
The period to wait for a response.
If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.

snapshot.create-repository.name: repository
snapshot.create-repository.description: The name of the repository for the snapshot.

snapshot.create-snapshot.name: snapshot
snapshot.create-snapshot.description:
The name of the snapshot.
It supportes date math.
It must be unique in the repository.

snapshot.create-master_timeout.name: master_timeout
snapshot.create-master_timeout.description:
The period to wait for a connection to the master node.
If no response is received before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.

snapshot.create-wait_for_completion.name: wait_for_completion
snapshot.create-wait_for_completion.description:
If `true`, the request returns a response when the snapshot is complete.
If `false`, the request returns a response when the snapshot initializes.

snapshot.create_repository-repository.name: repository
snapshot.create_repository-repository.description: The name of the snapshot repository to register or update.

snapshot.create_repository-master_timeou.name: master_timeout
snapshot.create_repository-master_timeou.description:
The period to wait for the master node.
If the master node is not available before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.
To indicate that the request should never timeout, set it to `-1`.

snapshot.create_repository-timeout.name: timeout
snapshot.create_repository-timeout.description:
The period to wait for a response from all relevant nodes in the cluster after updating the cluster metadata.
If no response is received before the timeout expires, the cluster metadata update still applies but the response will indicate that it was not completely acknowledged.
To indicate that the request should never timeout, set it to `-1`.

snapshot.create_repository-verify.name: verify
snapshot.create_repository-verify.description:
If `true`, the request verifies the repository is functional on all master and data nodes in the cluster.
If `false`, this verification is skipped.
You can also perform this verification with the verify snapshot repository API.

snapshot.get_repository-repository.name: repository
snapshot.get_repository-repository.description:
A comma-separated list of snapshot repository names used to limit the request.
Wildcard (`*`) expressions are supported including combining wildcards with exclude patterns starting with `-`.

To get information about all snapshot repositories registered in the cluster, omit this parameter or use `*` or `_all`.

snapshot.get_repository-local.name: local
snapshot.get_repository-local.description:
If `true`, the request gets information from the local node only.
If `false`, the request gets information from the master node.

snapshot.get_repository-master_timeout.name: master_timeout
snapshot.get_repository-master_timeout.description:
The period to wait for the master node.
If the master node is not available before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.
To indicate that the request should never timeout, set it to `-1`.

snapshot.status-repository.name: repository
snapshot.status-repository.description:
The snapshot repository name used to limit the request.
It supports wildcards (`*`) if `<snapshot>` isn't specified.

snapshot.status-snapshot.name: snapshot
snapshot.status-snapshot.description:
A comma-separated list of snapshots to retrieve status for.
The default is currently running snapshots.
Wildcards (`*`) are not supported.

snapshot.status-ignore_unavailable.name: ignore_unavailable
snapshot.status-ignore_unavailable.description:
If `false`, the request returns an error for any snapshots that are unavailable.
If `true`, the request ignores snapshots that are unavailable, such as those that are corrupted or temporarily cannot be returned.

snapshot.status-master_timeout.name: master_timeout
snapshot.status-master_timeout.description:
The period to wait for the master node.
If the master node is not available before the timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.
To indicate that the request should never timeout, set it to `-1`.

sql.query-format.name: format
sql.query-format.description:
The format for the response.
You can also specify a format using the `Accept` HTTP header.
If you specify both this parameter and the `Accept` HTTP header, this parameter takes precedence.

tasks.cancel-actions.name: actions
tasks.cancel-actions.description: A comma-separated list or wildcard expression of actions that is used to limit the request.

tasks.cancel-nodes.name: nodes
tasks.cancel-nodes.description: A comma-separated list of node IDs or names that is used to limit the request.

tasks.cancel-parent_task_id.name: parent_task_id
tasks.cancel-parent_task_id.description: A parent task ID that is used to limit the tasks.

tasks.cancel-wait_for_completion.name: wait_for_completion
tasks.cancel-wait_for_completion.description: If true, the request blocks until all found tasks are complete.

terms_enum-index.name: index
terms_enum-index.description:
A comma-separated list of data streams, indices, and index aliases to search.
Wildcard (`*`) expressions are supported.
To search all data streams or indices, omit this parameter or use `*`  or `_all`.

termvectors-index.name: index
termvectors-index.description: The name of the index that contains the document.

termvectors-id.name: id
termvectors-id.description: A unique identifier for the document.

termvectors-fields.name: fields
termvectors-fields.description:
A comma-separated list or wildcard expressions of fields to include in the statistics.
It is used as the default list unless a specific field list is provided in the `completion_fields` or `fielddata_fields` parameters.

termvectors-field_statistics.name: field_statistics
termvectors-field_statistics.description:
If `true`, the response includes:

* The document count (how many documents contain this field).
* The sum of document frequencies (the sum of document frequencies for all terms in this field).
* The sum of total term frequencies (the sum of total term frequencies of each term in this field).

termvectors-offsets.name: offsets
termvectors-offsets.description: If `true`, the response includes term offsets.

termvectors-payloads.name: payloads
termvectors-payloads.description: If `true`, the response includes term payloads.

termvectors-positions.name: positions
termvectors-positions.description: If `true`, the response includes term positions.

termvectors-preference.name: preference
termvectors-preference.description:
The node or shard the operation should be performed on.
It is random by default.

termvectors-realtime.name: realtime
termvectors-realtime.description: If true, the request is real-time as opposed to near-real-time.

termvectors-routing.name: routing
termvectors-routing.description: A custom value that is used to route operations to a specific shard.

termvectors-term_statistics.name: term_statistics
termvectors-term_statistics.description:
If `true`, the response includes:

* The total term frequency (how often a term occurs in all documents).
* The document frequency (the number of documents containing the current term).

By default these values are not returned since term statistics can have a serious performance impact.

termvectors-version.name: version
termvectors-version.description: If `true`, returns the document version as part of a hit.

termvectors-version_type.name: version_type
termvectors-version_type.description:
The version type.

Supported values include:
  - `internal`: Use internal versioning that starts at 1 and increments with each update or delete.
  - `external`: Only index the document if the specified version is strictly higher than the version of the stored document or if there is no existing document.
  - `external_gte`: Only index the document if the specified version is equal or higher than the version of the stored document or if there is no existing document.
NOTE: The `external_gte` version type is meant for special use cases and should be used with care.
If used incorrectly, it can result in loss of data.
  - `force`: This option is deprecated because it can cause primary and replica shards to diverge.

text_structure.find_message_structure-co.name: column_names
text_structure.find_message_structure-co.description:
If the format is `delimited`, you can specify the column names in a comma-separated list.
If this parameter is not specified, the structure finder uses the column names from the header row of the text.
If the text does not have a header role, columns are named "column1", "column2", "column3", for example.

text_structure.find_message_structure-de.name: delimiter
text_structure.find_message_structure-de.description:
If you the format is `delimited`, you can specify the character used to delimit the values in each row.
Only a single character is supported; the delimiter cannot have multiple characters.
By default, the API considers the following possibilities: comma, tab, semi-colon, and pipe (`|`).
In this default scenario, all rows must have the same number of fields for the delimited format to be detected.
If you specify a delimiter, up to 10% of the rows can have a different number of columns than the first row.

text_structure.find_message_structure-ec.name: ecs_compatibility
text_structure.find_message_structure-ec.description:
The mode of compatibility with ECS compliant Grok patterns.
Use this parameter to specify whether to use ECS Grok patterns instead of legacy ones when the structure finder creates a Grok pattern.
This setting primarily has an impact when a whole message Grok pattern such as `%{CATALINALOG}` matches the input.
If the structure finder identifies a common structure but has no idea of meaning then generic field names such as `path`, `ipaddress`, `field1`, and `field2` are used in the `grok_pattern` output, with the intention that a user who knows the meanings rename these fields before using it.

text_structure.find_message_structure-ex.name: explain
text_structure.find_message_structure-ex.description: If this parameter is set to true, the response includes a field named `explanation`, which is an array of strings that indicate how the structure finder produced its result.

text_structure.find_message_structure-fo.name: format
text_structure.find_message_structure-fo.description:
The high level structure of the text.
By default, the API chooses the format.
In this default scenario, all rows must have the same number of fields for a delimited format to be detected.
If the format is `delimited` and the delimiter is not set, however, the API tolerates up to 5% of rows that have a different number of columns than the first row.

text_structure.find_message_structure-gr.name: grok_pattern
text_structure.find_message_structure-gr.description:
If the format is `semi_structured_text`, you can specify a Grok pattern that is used to extract fields from every message in the text.
The name of the timestamp field in the Grok pattern must match what is specified in the `timestamp_field` parameter.
If that parameter is not specified, the name of the timestamp field in the Grok pattern must match "timestamp".
If `grok_pattern` is not specified, the structure finder creates a Grok pattern.

text_structure.find_message_structure-qu.name: quote
text_structure.find_message_structure-qu.description:
If the format is `delimited`, you can specify the character used to quote the values in each row if they contain newlines or the delimiter character.
Only a single character is supported.
If this parameter is not specified, the default value is a double quote (`"`).
If your delimited text format does not use quoting, a workaround is to set this argument to a character that does not appear anywhere in the sample.

text_structure.find_message_structure-sh.name: should_trim_fields
text_structure.find_message_structure-sh.description:
If the format is `delimited`, you can specify whether values between delimiters should have whitespace trimmed from them.
If this parameter is not specified and the delimiter is pipe (`|`), the default value is true.
Otherwise, the default value is `false`.

text_structure.find_message_structure-ti.name: timeout
text_structure.find_message_structure-ti.description:
The maximum amount of time that the structure analysis can take.
If the analysis is still running when the timeout expires, it will be stopped.

text_structure.find_message_structure-ti.name: timestamp_field
text_structure.find_message_structure-ti.description:
The name of the field that contains the primary timestamp of each record in the text.
In particular, if the text was ingested into an index, this is the field that would be used to populate the `@timestamp` field.

If the format is `semi_structured_text`, this field must match the name of the appropriate extraction in the `grok_pattern`.
Therefore, for semi-structured text, it is best not to specify this parameter unless `grok_pattern` is also specified.

For structured text, if you specify this parameter, the field must exist within the text.

If this parameter is not specified, the structure finder makes a decision about which field (if any) is the primary timestamp field.
For structured text, it is not compulsory to have a timestamp in the text.

text_structure.find_message_structure-ti.name: timestamp_format
text_structure.find_message_structure-ti.description:
The Java time format of the timestamp field in the text.
Only a subset of Java time format letter groups are supported:

* `a`
* `d`
* `dd`
* `EEE`
* `EEEE`
* `H`
* `HH`
* `h`
* `M`
* `MM`
* `MMM`
* `MMMM`
* `mm`
* `ss`
* `XX`
* `XXX`
* `yy`
* `yyyy`
* `zzz`

Additionally `S` letter groups (fractional seconds) of length one to nine are supported providing they occur after `ss` and are separated from the `ss` by a period (`.`), comma (`,`), or colon (`:`).
Spacing and punctuation is also permitted with the exception a question mark (`?`), newline, and carriage return, together with literal text enclosed in single quotes.
For example, `MM/dd HH.mm.ss,SSSSSS 'in' yyyy` is a valid override format.

One valuable use case for this parameter is when the format is semi-structured text, there are multiple timestamp formats in the text, and you know which format corresponds to the primary timestamp, but you do not want to specify the full `grok_pattern`.
Another is when the timestamp format is one that the structure finder does not consider by default.

If this parameter is not specified, the structure finder chooses the best format from a built-in set.

If the special value `null` is specified, the structure finder will not look for a primary timestamp in the text.
When the format is semi-structured text, this will result in the structure finder treating the text as single-line messages.

text_structure.test_grok_pattern-ecs_com.name: ecs_compatibility
text_structure.test_grok_pattern-ecs_com.description:
The mode of compatibility with ECS compliant Grok patterns.
Use this parameter to specify whether to use ECS Grok patterns instead of legacy ones when the structure finder creates a Grok pattern.
Valid values are `disabled` and `v1`.

transform.get_transform-transform_id.name: transform_id
transform.get_transform-transform_id.description:
Identifier for the transform. It can be a transform identifier or a
wildcard expression. You can get information for all transforms by using
`_all`, by specifying `*` as the `<transform_id>`, or by omitting the
`<transform_id>`.

transform.get_transform-allow_no_match.name: allow_no_match
transform.get_transform-allow_no_match.description:
Specifies what to do when the request:

1. Contains wildcard expressions and there are no transforms that match.
2. Contains the _all string or no identifiers and there are no matches.
3. Contains wildcard expressions and there are only partial matches.

If this parameter is false, the request returns a 404 status code when
there are no matches or only partial matches.

transform.get_transform-from.name: from
transform.get_transform-from.description: Skips the specified number of transforms.

transform.get_transform-size.name: size
transform.get_transform-size.description: Specifies the maximum number of transforms to obtain.

transform.get_transform-exclude_generate.name: exclude_generated
transform.get_transform-exclude_generate.description:
Excludes fields that were automatically added when creating the
transform. This allows the configuration to be in an acceptable format to
be retrieved and then added to another cluster.

transform.preview_transform-transform_id.name: transform_id
transform.preview_transform-transform_id.description:
Identifier for the transform to preview. If you specify this path parameter, you cannot provide transform
configuration details in the request body.

transform.preview_transform-timeout.name: timeout
transform.preview_transform-timeout.description:
Period to wait for a response. If no response is received before the
timeout expires, the request fails and returns an error.

watcher.ack_watch-action_id.description:

watcher.execute_watch-debug.name: debug
watcher.execute_watch-debug.description: Defines whether the watch runs in debug mode.

watcher.put_watch-active.name: active
watcher.put_watch-active.description:

The default value is `true`, which means the watch is active by default.

watcher.put_watch-if_primary_term.name: if_primary_term

watcher.put_watch-if_seq_no.name: if_seq_no
watcher.put_watch-if_seq_no.description: only update the watch if the last operation that has changed the watch has the specified sequence number

watcher.put_watch-version.name: version
watcher.put_watch-version.description: Explicit version number for concurrency control

watcher.stats-emit_stacktraces.name: emit_stacktraces

index_filter.description:
Filter indices if the provided query rewrites to `match_none` on every shard.

IMPORTANT: The filtering is done on a best-effort basis, it uses index statistics and mappings to rewrite queries to `match_none` instead of fully running the request.
For instance a range query over a date field can rewrite to `match_none` if all documents within a shard (including deleted documents) are outside of the provided range.
However, not all queries can rewrite to `match_none` so this API may return an index even if the provided filter matches no document.

composed_of.description:

Component templates are merged in the order specified, meaning that the last component template specified has the highest precedence.

template.description:

It may optionally include an `aliases`, `mappings`, or `settings` configuration.

data_stream.description:
If this object is included, the template is used to create data streams and their backing indices.
Supports an empty object.
Data streams require a matching index template with a `data_stream` object.

priority.description:
Priority to determine index template precedence when a new data stream or index is created.
The index template with the highest priority is chosen.
If no priority is specified the template is treated as though it is of priority 0 (lowest priority).
This number is not automatically generated by Elasticsearch.

version.description:
Version number used to manage index templates externally.
This number is not automatically generated by Elasticsearch.
External systems can use these version numbers to simplify template management.
To unset a version, replace the template without specifying one.

_meta.description:
Optional user metadata about the index template.
It may have any contents.
It is not automatically generated or used by Elasticsearch.
This user-defined object is stored in the cluster state, so keeping it short is preferable

allow_auto_create.description:
This setting overrides the value of the `action.auto_create_index` cluster setting.
If set to `true` in a template, then indices can be automatically created using that template even if auto-creation of indices is disabled via `actions.auto_create_index`.
If set to `false`, then indices or data streams matching the template must always be explicitly created, and may never be automatically created.

context.description:
The context that the script should run in.
NOTE: Result ordering in the field contexts is not guaranteed.

Supported values include:
  - `painless_test`: The default context if no other context is specified.
  - `filter`: Treats scripts as if they were run inside a script query.
  - `score`: Treats scripts as if they were run inside a `script_score` function in a `function_score` query.
  - `boolean_field`: The context for boolean fields. The script returns a `true` or `false` response.
  - `date_field`: The context for date fields. `emit` takes a long value and the script returns a sorted list of dates.
  - `double_field`: The context for double numeric fields. The script returns a sorted list of double values.
  - `geo_point_field`: The context for geo-point fields. `emit` takes two double parameters, the latitude and longitude values, and the script returns an object in GeoJSON format containing the coordinates for the geo point.
  - `ip_field`: The context for `ip` fields. The script returns a sorted list of IP addresses.
  - `keyword_field`: The context for keyword fields. The script returns a sorted list of string values.
  - `long_field`: The context for long numeric fields. The script returns a sorted list of long values.
  - `composite_field`: The context for composite runtime fields. The script returns a map of values.

For testing purposes, a document must be provided so that it will be temporarily indexed in-memory and is accessible from the script. More precisely, the `_source`, stored fields, and doc values of such a document are available to the script being tested.

aggregations.description: Defines the aggregations that are run as part of the search request.

collapse.description: Collapses search results the values of the specified field.

explain.description: If `true`, the request returns detailed information about score computation as part of a hit.

ext.description: Configuration of search extensions defined by Elasticsearch plugins.

from.description:
The starting document offset, which must be non-negative.
By default, you cannot page through more than 10,000 hits using the `from` and `size` parameters.
To page through more hits, use the `search_after` parameter.

highlight.description: Specifies the highlighter to use for retrieving highlighted snippets from one or more fields in your search results.

track_total_hits.description:
Number of hits matching the query to count accurately.
If `true`, the exact number of hits is returned at the cost of some performance.
If `false`, the  response does not include the total number of hits matching the query.

indices_boost.description:
Boost the `_score` of documents from specified indices.
The boost value is the factor by which scores are multiplied.
A boost value greater than `1.0` increases the score.
A boost value between `0` and `1.0` decreases the score.
